back.title: What changes the answer?
back.html:
The short-horizon comparison favors renting because transaction costs have little time to spread out.
  • Longer stay can spread buying and selling costs.
  • Higher rent growth can favor buying.
  • Repairs, price declines and investing the down payment can favor renting.
  • Space, stability and flexibility may matter more than the modeled dollars.
Run several plausible scenarios.

questions.prompt: Evaluate the claim: “Renting is always a waste of money.”
questions.answer: Sometimes true — it depends on the situation

options.text: Always true
Sometimes true — it depends on the situation
Never true

solutionSteps: Sometimes true — renting can cost more than buying for someone who stays in one home for many years in a rising market. But owners also pay unrecoverable costs (interest, property tax, insurance, maintenance, transaction costs) and give up returns on the down payment, so for shorter stays renting is often the cheaper choice. It is not always a waste.
